simulate.description: Run one ngspice batch simulation (ngspice -b) of a deck. Inputs: deck (path relative to the design root; the deck holds the circuit, the analyses and a .control block), libs (optional list of {path, section}; each becomes a .lib line before the deck, for example a PDK corner; $PDK_ROOT is expanded), measurements (optional {name: unit}). A measurement is read from a 'name = value' line in the ngspice output, so use meas or print in the .control block with the same name. A wanted name that ngspice does not print is reported as missing. params (optional {name: number or string}) and temp_c (optional number) become .param and .temp lines after the deck, so they replace the deck's values. A sweep bench prints one line per point, 'ROW <sweep>=<v> <name>=<value> ...' (echo in a foreach loop); the response then has <name>.min and <name>.max with 'at', the sweep point, and work/sweep.json has the table. A point without a value makes .min and .max failed. Files that the deck writes (for example with wrdata) go to the work directory of the experiment and are hashed. The response has a warning for each simulator option that adds elements to the circuit (rshunt, cshunt, a gmin above 1e-12), with its file and line.

operating_point.description: Find the DC operating point of each MOS device of a testbench, and whether it is in saturation. Inputs: deck and libs, as for simulate; technology (optional, the name of a technology pack; the default is the pack for $PDK). The adapter removes the .control blocks, the analyses and the .meas lines of the deck, and runs 'op' at the DC values of the sources in the netlist. To check one condition (for example one input common-mode voltage or one corner), set the DC values and the libs for that condition. The response has, for each MOS device, the measurements <device>.vgs, .vth, .vds, .vdsat, .id, .gm, .gds, .vov (|vgs| - |vth|) and .sat_margin (|vds| - |vdsat|), all as magnitudes for PMOS too, and a warning for each device in triode (sat_margin < 0) or subthreshold (vov < 0). work/operating_point.json has the region of each device. Use it to find why a design fails, before you change a size. Run it at the condition that fails (the corner in libs and the DC values of the failing point, for example the end of an input range), not only at the nominal condition: a device can be in saturation at tt and in triode at ss.

lint.description: Check netlists without a simulation. Inputs: files (list of netlist paths relative to the design root). The response has the same option warnings as simulate, for each file and the files that it includes from the design root.

check_design.description: Check a design netlist against its design contract, without a simulation. check_requirements runs it for the design section of requirements.json. Inputs: file (relative to the design root), subckt, pins (in order), elements (allowed kinds, "mos", "r", "c"; default all), devices (the allowed devices of the technology pack; default all; a name that the pack does not have fails the run), limits ({gate_area_um2, r_ohm, c_f}, maxima), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK). Rules: the file holds only .subckt blocks without parameters. In a block, an X line instantiates a MOS device of the technology pack that devices allows (with plain-number sizes at or above the minimum) or another block of the file; R and C lines have 4 fields and a plain positive value. Sources, M lines, .model, .include, .lib, .param, .option and {expressions} are errors. The response status is completed also when the design has errors; each error is an error diagnostic with its file and line. Measurements: gate_area_um2 (sum of W x L x m of all MOS devices, hierarchy expanded), mos_count, design_errors. work/design.json has the errors and the elements.
